draft.title: Evaluating representations of concepts
card: A representation is the way a text presents a concept, such as success or justice. A text shows one version of the concept. It does not show the whole of it.
Fairly
Ask whether the text treats the concept even-handedly, or pushes one side by leaving out other views or using loaded words.
Fully
Ask how much of the concept the text covers. A text that defines success only as money leaves out other ideas of success, such as health or friendship.
Context
A text is shaped by when, where and for whom it was made. Its context can explain why it represents a concept the way it does.
draft.remember: Judge a representation by how fair and how full it is, and link it to its context.

a.q: A school magazine article says a person is successful only if they earn a high salary. Which judgement about its representation of success is best?
opts: It is narrow, as it leaves out other kinds of success
It is full, as money is the only real kind of success
It is fair, as the article is about a school magazine
It is accurate, as it uses a clear and simple definition
a.why: The article covers only one idea of success, so it is not a full representation. The tempting option says it is full, but a single measure leaves out other ideas such as health or friendship.
a.clue: Ask how much of the concept the article covers.

b.q: A 1950s poster shows justice as a stern judge who always punishes wrongdoers and never shows mercy. Which response best evaluates the poster?
opts: It shows one view of justice, which may reflect its era
It shows the full meaning of justice for every era
It is fair because posters must be simple and direct
It cannot be judged because it is only a poster
b.why: The poster presents justice as punishment alone, so it is a partial view. Its context, the era it was made in, may help explain that view. The option about posters being simple is tempting, but a simple message can still be unfair or narrow.
b.clue: Think about how full the view is, and when it was made.

a.best: It is narrow, as it leaves out other kinds of success

b.best: It shows one view of justice, which may reflect its era

b.q: A 1950s poster shows justice as a stern judge who always punishes wrongdoers and never shows mercy. Which response best evaluates the poster?
opts: A narrow view of justice that its era may help explain
A full view of justice that its era may help explain
A narrow view of justice that its era cannot help explain
A full view of justice that every era would agree with
